convoLines.text: "We're eating through stores faster than we replace them. Forage with me tomorrow? I know the south slope below the meadow."
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. I know the south slope below the meadow — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Rocco is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Alright, duty calls. This was a good pause."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"...Hi. Sorry. I'm not good at the talking-to-strangers part. It'll pass."
Something eases in their shoulders. "Oh. Okay. That's... that's fine, then."
"Strangers are just people you haven't disappointed yet. That's what my mother said. Terrible advice, but it got me through parties."
"What if it's art? Like — the whole thing. We're not an experiment, we're a medium. It's sculpting us."
"Take your time."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on the big questions. Just thinking out loud."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Anyway — I should get going."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
Everything's broken — bodies, tools, people. I fix things. It's what I'm for.
"Healing's slow. People want it fast. I'm learning to be patient with both."
"Hurt people hurt people. Somebody has to break the chain. Might as well be me."
"Still on what they want."
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
"Right. Sorry, I go on about it. What did you want?"

"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Have you heard what they're calling Highbeam Deer? Manuel is pushing 'Sir Blinds-A-Lot'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
You show them Cattail — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
Mariana: "You. Yeah, you. What do you make of this?"
"Take your time."
A warmth settles over the conversation — they lean in a little.
"Got a read on anyone here yet? Who should I be watching? Seen worse."
"Okay, but what about Same. But keep your eyes open — some people here are performing, not surviving."
"Still on your read on people here."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Good question." "The whole fire was arguing about Highbeam Deer last night — what to even CALL it. 'Sir Blinds-A-Lot' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Okay. You don't have to have an answer."
"I'm staying out of the naming fight. For now. Someone always gets precious about their pick."
"I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"Can I tell you something? I've been writing letters I'll never send. I'm ashamed and I can't stop."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
Tariq shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on their secret."
"Has this changed you? Like, fundamentally?"
"The old you got you here. The new you keeps you here. Both count."
"I'd love to. Lead the way." (They're already checking your pack.)
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
Lucas: "Don't just stand there — you've got opinions, right?"
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
It's quiet at the tree line. Lucas doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. I know the south slope below the meadow — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on their request."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Yeah? What's up?"

"You want to know about that? Okay." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "The whole fire was arguing about Hushpuppy last night — what to even CALL it. 'The Ugly Beast' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"My cut needs a second pair of hands. Will you help me clean it?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"BROTHERS! That's The Union Rep telling you it's about to move. It hunts by day — watch the open ground."
"Ugly-Eyes — It lands. It hunts at night — give the dark a wide berth."
"We went over this," Manuel says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"...Okay. I'll figure it out." They won't ask twice. That much is clear.
"Still on that favor."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Okay. I'll manage on my own."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You said you're still figuring everyone out. Figure anything out yet? Anyone you're watching?"
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
You walk to the ridge with Mariana. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that personal stuff."
A beat. Then, as if shaking something off:
"Sure — what's on your mind? …if that makes sense."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Everyone's choosing sides and pretending they aren't. I hate it."
"I talk to both sides. It hasn't exploded yet."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"What's the kindest thing someone's done for you out here? Trust me. Mostly."
"Funny thing: That's the good stuff. Quiet generosity. It's holding this whole thing together."
"Watch for this: It drops its head and paws the earth — once, twice — and the dust comes up in a wall. Dustboar, every time. It hunts by day — watch the open ground."
"Someone saved me the last of the stew once. Didn't say anything, just put the bowl down and walked off. I think about that bowl more than I think about the monsters."
"It gave us a codex. You know what that tells me? It expects us to need one. Plan accordingly."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Jerusalem Artichoke — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Yeah? What's up? Makes sense to me."
"You want to know what I did in the raid? I stood down Big-Eyes at the treeline — it ran. Don't call it brave. Call it awake."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to that favor."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You said you're not good at the talking part either. For what it's worth — you're doing fine."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Like I said — Still on that personal stuff. …sorry."
A pause. When they speak again, it's about something else entirely.
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "You feel that? The air before a storm. That's the village right now."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
